subject: humanities
passage: Most monumental temples are built up from the ground, stone laid upon stone. The Kailasa temple at Ellora, in the Indian state of Maharashtra, was made in the opposite way. Beginning in the eighth century, workers cut deep trenches into a basalt hillside and then carved downward, freeing an entire temple, with its towers, halls, and sculpted elephants, from a single mass of rock. Such a method allowed no correction: a misjudged cut could not be undone by replacing a stone. Historians have estimated that around 200,000 metric tons of rock were removed, and they continue to debate how the builders planned the work so precisely, since no detailed plans from the period survive.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It contrasts the usual way of making a building with one temple's method and considers its demands.
choices.B: It describes a temple's towers and sculptures and then explains how historians measured its size.
choices.C: It explains a building method and then argues that it was more efficient than building upward.
choices.D: It presents the builders' surviving plans and then describes how the workers departed from them in places.

explanation.why: The text opens with the usual method (building "up from the ground") and says Kailasa "was made in the opposite way." After describing the carving, it considers what this required: no room for correction, huge amounts of rock removed, and precise planning that historians still debate.
explanation.A: Correct. The text sets ordinary construction against carving downward and then discusses the precision and planning this method required.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The towers and sculptures are mentioned in passing, and the text does not explain how historians measured anything.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text never claims the method was efficient; it stresses how unforgiving and demanding it was.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says "no detailed plans from the period survive," so it cannot present the builders' plans.
